elements.element: Renewal occurs only by mutual written agreement, or alternatively automatic 12-month renewal terms
elements.evidence: "shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof" — evergreen term with no renewal mechanic, so no auto-renewal is imposed on Company (condition absent)

elements.element: If automatic renewal: Customer opt-out on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: No automatic renewal exists ("continue until terminated by either party"); either party may terminate under Paragraph 6, so the opt-out requirement is conditionally absent

elements.element: If automatic renewal: Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal
elements.evidence: No renewal date exists to remind against; term runs "until terminated by either party" — condition demonstrably absent

elements.element: Price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: "Any change in Contractor's rates shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index and 3%."

elements.element: Automatic renewal with non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: No auto-renewal; termination available to either party and Contractor's rate-change notice is "30 days notice to Company" (≤60 days)
Cap of "the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index and 3%" is within 5%

reasons: The inserted sentence supplies exactly the preferred price-escalation cap ("lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index and 3%"), the only preferred element the clause was missing.

The renewal-specific elements (opt-out notice, 60-day reminder) are conditionally absent: the term is evergreen and terminable by either party under Paragraph 6, so no auto-renewal exists to opt out of or be reminded about.
Minimality is satisfied: a single concise sentence appended after the rate-change right, with no rewrite of the existing 30-day notice right and no fallback-only 5% figure imported.

Intent preserved: invoicing detail, expense support, and Contractor's 30-day notice right remain fully effective; the cap simply constrains the magnitude of any increase. Note only that "Consumer Price Index" is not defined in the Agreement — a drafting nicety worth raising in the rationale, not a material deviation.
